An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: ECf 30
div.ab: Euerwichescyre, Nicolescyre, Notingehamscyre, Leircestrescyre, Northamtunescyre, usque ad Watlingestret et VIII ultra Watlingestret sub lege Anglorum.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 652 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.
Liebermann’s upright (roman) letter a after “usque” refers to his explanatory notes, the Erklärungen (printed as Gesetze III; his note on p. 627 calls it “Band II”), which are not yet added here.
Liebermann’s letter after “usque” is his upright a (Erklärungen).
